audience.text: Developers building 3D applications in Node.js who need to construct, traverse, and convert scene graphs using TypeScript or JavaScript without native dependencies.

capabilities.text: Construct hierarchical 3D scenes using Scene, Node, and Entity types with support for transforms, materials, and child hierarchies.
capabilities.title: Scene graph construction

capabilities.text: Create mesh geometry with control points, polygons, and vertex attribute channels including normals, UVs, and vertex colors.
capabilities.title: Mesh geometry creation

capabilities.text: Assign shading materials including LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, and PbrMaterial with texture mapping support.
capabilities.title: Material assignment

capabilities.text: Add Camera and Light entities to scenes with configurable projection types, field of view, clip planes, and light types.
capabilities.title: Camera and light entities

capabilities.text: Animate node properties using keyframe sequences with configurable interpolation, extrapolation, and binding points.
capabilities.title: Animation support

capabilities.text: Read and write multiple 3D formats including glTF, OBJ, STL, FBX, COLLADA, and 3MF through dedicated importers and exporters.
capabilities.title: Format I/O

capabilities.text: Perform 2D/3D/4D vector operations, matrix math, and geometric calculations using dedicated math utility classes.
capabilities.title: Math utilities

capabilities.text: Manage metadata and custom properties on scene objects using the Property and PropertyCollection APIs.
capabilities.title: Property system

limitations.text: Rendering is not implemented — Scene.render() throws an error.
Boolean operations on meshes (union, difference, intersect), optimize(), and isManifold() throw 'not implemented' errors.
VertexElement.setIndices() and clear() throw 'not implemented' errors.
Node.selectSingleObject() and selectObjects() throw 'not implemented' errors.
The FileSystem abstraction methods (readFile, writeFile, createZipFileSystem, etc.) are unimplemented and throw errors.
OBJ export only writes geometry attached at the root node and does not write material data in a readable form.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic construction of 3D scenes with hierarchical nodes, meshes, materials, cameras, and lights using a consistent API.
Supports reading and writing common 3D interchange formats including glTF, OBJ, STL, FBX, COLLADA, and 3MF.
Provides animation support through keyframe sequences, animation channels, and clips for node property interpolation.
Offers utilities for mesh triangulation, bounding box calculations, and vector/matrix math operations.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for TypeScript is a free, open-source TypeScript library for building, converting, and manipulating 3D scenes in Node.js, exposing an Aspose.3D-compatible scene-graph API.

uncertainties: OBJ import does not assign per-face materials from source files regardless of load options — behavior not fully documented.
Re-importing exported glTF scenes can produce extra duplicate top-level nodes — root cause unclear.
Text watermarking is not functional — identical to a defect on the 3d/net platform, but implementation details not provided.
3MF import/export has a real npm packaging defect — runtime dependency missing in published package.
Binary GLB export fails for non-empty meshes — JSON/ASCII export unaffected, but cause not specified.
VertexFieldSemantic and VertexFieldDataType enum values exist but usage in vertex element construction is not demonstrated.
Watermark.encodeWatermark and Watermark.decodeWatermark exist but no examples show their usage or integration.
The package.json entry point does not match the actual build output — examples import from dist/ instead of package name.

workflows.name: Load and save 3D scenes
workflows.text: Load a scene from a file or buffer using Scene.open() or Scene.openFromBuffer(), then save it to another format using Scene.save() or Scene.saveToBuffer().

workflows.name: Build mesh geometry
workflows.text: Create a Mesh, add control points, and define polygons using Mesh.addControlPoint() and Mesh.createPolygon(), then attach vertex attribute elements like UVs and normals.

workflows.name: Assign materials
workflows.text: Instantiate material subclasses such as LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial, configure their properties, and assign them to nodes via Node.materials.

workflows.name: Create animations
workflows.text: Build AnimationClip objects containing AnimationNode tracks with AnimationChannel bindings to node properties, populated with KeyframeSequence data.

workflows.name: Triangulate geometry
workflows.text: Triangulate raw polygon data using PolygonModifier.triangulate() or in-place on a Mesh using Mesh.triangulate().

workflows.name: Inspect scene hierarchy
workflows.text: Traverse the scene graph starting from Scene.rootNode, accessing child nodes, entities, and transforms recursively.
